title: test_qos_wrr_floor_zero_share never creates a zero-share lane — its {100,1,1} weights exceed MAX_WEIGHT (64), are silently rejected, and the E7 floor path is never exercised
detail: The test claims to pin the E7 WRR floor (a zero-allocation lane still drains) but the weight command is rejected, so every lane has cap >= 1 and the assertion passes through ordinary service. The floor branch in flow.odin has no real coverage.
recommended_fix: Use legal weights that still round Standard to zero (e.g. {64,1,1} on capacity 5), and make submit_c fail the test on a rejected command so a rejected fixture edit can never go silent again.

title: The severance-with-alternative tests don't pin in-flight rerouting — fresh spawns mask it, and the captured drop counter is discarded
evidence:
if del_after <= del_before { tfail(t, "reroute must keep deliveries flowing") }
	_ = sev_drops_before  — with sev_drops_before captured at line 73 ('sev_drops_before := state.flow.sla[streaming].dropped') and never asserted. Post-demolish, flow_step spawns 30 packets/tick that BFS onto the surviving router->j2->h1 path at spawn time, so deliveries increase even if every mid-edge packet had dropped. The twin test in flow_test.odin:149 has the same shape: 'if delivered_after <= delivered_before { tfail(t, "reroute must keep deliveries flowing") }'.
detail: E1 branch 1 (mid-edge packets reroute from their current node) has no effective assertion: the delivered-total comparison is satisfied by fresh spawns alone. The discarded sev_drops_before shows the intended Severance-drop check was abandoned.
recommended_fix: Assert dropped stays flat across the demolish in the with-alt case (no Ev_Packet_Dropped{.Severance}, dropped == sev_drops_before), which only holds if mid-edge packets actually reroute.

title: Severance tests hardcode the direct leg as pipe id 2 while the fixture computes and discards the real id
evidence:
Fixture (core/flow_edge_test.odin:36-45): 'nb, direct, _ := topology_apply_edit(&state.topology,
		Command{kind = Cmd_Draw_Pipe{a = router, b = h1, tier = std}}, cat, state.budget, 1) ... _ = direct' — then both tests re-derive the id as a literal: 'direct := u32(2)' (lines 62 and 93).
detail: The Edit_Result already carries res.pipe, but the fixture throws it away and the tests depend on the fixture's draw order (boot pipe 1, then this leg). Any reorder silently demolishes the wrong pipe.
recommended_fix: Return the direct pipe id from severance_fixture (res.pipe) instead of discarding it, and drop the u32(2) literals.
